issues.detail: The Hebrew has 'שִׁמְשַׁי סָפְרָא' (Shimshai the scribe), but the Chinese renders '希實米人書記官' which appears to be a different name ('希實米' is not Shimshai). This is a name swap/error.

The Hebrew 'פִּתְגָמָא שְׁלַח מַלְכָּא' means 'the king sent a message/letter'; the Chinese '王發出書信' is fine, but the phrase 'עַל רְחוּם בְּעֵל טְעֵם' is 'to Rehum the commander' — the Chinese '宰相利宏' renders '利宏' for Rehum, but '宰相' (prime minister) is an addition not in the Hebrew; 'בְּעֵל טְעֵם' means 'lord of decree/commander', not '宰相'. This is an addition/mistranslation.
